keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Atmospheric Australian coastal rock in G major balancing laid-back surf-coast strums with haunting minor-key storytelling
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: A breezy two-chord pendulum (G - C) throughout the verses that gracefully gives way to the emotional release of the Em - C - G - D chorus hook.

sectionProgressions.description: Hypnotic two-chord swing with open ringing strings and lush analog chorus modulation
Iconic Australian singalong ('Meet me down by the jetty...') pivoting through the relative minor Em to open D
Pensive supertonic Am turnaround setting up the melodic guitar solo

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Warm acoustic home base evoking the Australian coastline and open road
C (IV) - Bright subdominant lift rocking back and forth against the G tonic
Em (vi) - Relative minor providing sudden emotional depth and poignancy in the chorus
D (V) - Dominant anchor resolving tension at the end of each chorus phrase
Am (ii) - Darker minor substitution coloring the reflective bridge section

techniques.name: Lush Chorus Arpeggiation & Open-String Ringing
techniques.description: Gentle fingerpicked and flatpicked arpeggios allowing open high E and B strings to ring freely with analog chorus modulation

sequence: Keep your ring and pinky fingers anchored on the 3rd fret of strings 1 and 2
Shift your index and middle fingers between G, Cadd9, and Em7 shapes
Strum with a fluid, relaxed down-up motion at 108 BPM
tips: Anchoring fingers 3 and 4 provides a seamless pedal point between all chord changes
Use a thin to medium pick (0.60mm) for smooth acoustic strumming without harsh string attack
Add an analog chorus pedal (Boss CE-2) for the signature 1983 coastal sparkle

techniques.name: Simon Binks Weeping Volume Swells & Sliding 6ths
techniques.description: Evocative, vocal-like sliding 6th intervals across strings 1 and 3 combined with smooth guitar volume knob swells and analog chorus

notes: Sliding 6ths on strings 3 and 1: 4/3 -> 7/7 -> 9/8 -> 11/10 -> 12/12
Mute the middle 2nd string with the underside of your index finger
Pinky volume swells: strike note with volume at 0, then roll up to 10 for violin-like attack
sequence: Fret the 6th intervals with fingers 1 (string 1) and 2 or 3 (string 3)
Slide into each harmony position with gentle fret-hand vibrato
Let the notes bloom into the stereo analog chorus and plate reverb wash
tips: Use a Stratocaster in the neck/middle out-of-phase switch position for warm, liquid chime
Keep the right hand picking very soft; let the amplifier's headroom provide sustain
Listen to the Mornington Peninsula seaside atmosphere to internalize the languid, weeping phrasing

sections.name: Intro Ambient Acoustic-Electric Chime
sections.description: Breezy coastal acoustic strumming layered with Simon Binks's chiming, chorus-drenched Stratocaster arpeggios.
notes: Keep the high D and G pedal notes ringing continuously on strings 1 and 2
Pluck the inner strings softly to establish the relaxed pendulum feel
Engage lush stereo chorus (Boss CE-2) for the authentic 1983 shimmer

sections.name: Verse 1 Coastal Pendulum
sections.description: James Reyne's unmistakable slurred vocal phrasing begins over the relaxed G to Cadd9 pendulum.
notes: Keep the high D and G pedal notes ringing continuously
Strum with light, relaxed downstrokes at 108 BPM
Leave dynamic space under James Reyne's storytelling vocal

sections.name: Chorus 'Down by the Jetty'
sections.description: The immortal 'Meet me down by the jetty' chorus progression, with ringing pedal tones on strings 1 and 2.
notes: Dig in with slightly fuller strumming dynamics on the Em7 drop
Keep fingers 3 and 4 anchored at fret 3 for seamless transitions
Clean, crisp open D major resolution on beat 4

sections.name: Bridge Supertonic Turnaround
sections.description: Reflective bridge detour stepping through Am and C, creating dynamic contrast before launching into Simon Binks's guitar solo.
notes: Ease back on pick velocity for an intimate, moody acoustic timbre
Let the open high E string shimmer over the Am and C shapes
Sustain the open D chord to set up the solo entrance

sections.name: Simon Binks's Weeping Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Simon Binks Weeping Volume Swells & Sliding 6ths
sections.description: One of the most expressive guitar solos in Australian music history. Simon Binks plays weeping sliding 6ths on strings 1 and 3, gentle volume swells, and vocal-like G major pentatonic bends that evoke the sound of waves lapping on the Mornington Peninsula jetty.
notes: Slide gently between the 6th intervals: 4/3 -> 7/7 -> 9/8 on strings 3 and 1
Ascend into the 11/10 and 12/12 positions with sweet finger vibrato
Hit the 15th-fret B string note with a crying whole-step bend and slow release
Resolve back to the warm open G chord as the rhythm section rejoins

sections.name: Outro Coastal Jam & Fade
sections.description: Extended seaside outro jam with Simon Binks weaving delicate, weeping Stratocaster licks around Reyne's fading vocal repetitions.
notes: Keep the G to Cadd9 pendulum strumming with light, relaxed dynamics
Weave sweet pentatonic fills at the 12th fret between vocal phrases
Let the analog chorus and delay repeats gently fade out

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (Simon Binks) or Maton Acoustic Dreadnought
guitar.pickup: Neck/middle out-of-phase position for shimmering cleans

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus or Fender Twin Reverb

effects.distortion: Clean boost or light transparent overdrive
effects.other: Analog Stereo Chorus (Boss CE-2) and subtle analog delay

beginner.title: Anchored Open Chords
steps: Learn the G, Cadd9, Em7, and Dsus4 anchored chord grip (fingers 3 & 4 on fret 3)
Practice smooth two-finger shifts between G and Cadd9
Strum along with the recording at 108 BPM
beginner.goals: Flawless transitions between the four main chords

intermediate.title: Acoustic-Electric Dynamics & Groove
steps: Master the subtle 16th-note strumming groove with offbeat accents
Practice Simon Binks's atmospheric electric guitar arpeggios
Lock in with the bass and drums at 108 BPM using our Metronome
intermediate.goals: Authentic Australian Crawl coastal vibe and dynamic touch

advanced.title: Simon Binks Melodic Solo
steps: Learn Simon Binks's lyrical guitar solo blending G major and E minor pentatonic
Master the smooth sliding 6th intervals across strings 1 and 3
Incorporate subtle volume swells and tremolo bar vibrato
advanced.goals: Complete song playthrough including studio-accurate lead solo

commonMistakes: Lifting fingers 3 and 4 during chord changes instead of keeping them anchored
Strumming too aggressively on the verse which drowns out the atmospheric vocals
Rushing the tempo past 108 BPM on the chorus singalong
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 5 minutes of anchored G - Cadd9 - Em7 - Dsus4 chord cycles
Practice light-touch strumming with a 0.60mm pick along with a metronome
Work on Simon Binks's intro arpeggios with chorus and delay engaged
focusAreas: Relaxed strumming hand with loose wrist rotation
Sustaining the ringing high D and G drone notes across changes
Dynamic sensitivity between verse whisper and chorus roar
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM with our metronome tool set to 8th-note subdivisions
Practice holding steady time during the long ambient instrumental outro
